## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `EscalationTrigger` is a union of `tms_unavailable`, `tms_timeout`, `no_tool_for_question`, `customer_asked_for_human`, `out_of_scope_change_request`; a `switch` over it with no `default` compiles, failing `npm run typecheck` if a trigger is added without a matching case elsewhere
- [ ] A tool call returning `unavailable` or `timeout` marks an escalation with no model action - tested with a mock provider emitting no `escalate_to_human` call, asserting one record exists
- [ ] A `not_found` from the same fixture marks no escalation
- [ ] `escalate_to_human` is registered, declares exactly one required enum-constrained `reason_category`; a call with an invalid value is rejected by `037`'s validation as a readable tool result, not a throw, with a `stream_end`

## What to do

Add `apps/api/src/escalation/`: `triggers.ts` (an `EscalationTrigger` union), `escalationRecorder.ts` (`mark` during a turn, `flush` at the end of it), `escalationSink.ts` (the port - `deliver(record)`), `recordOnlySink.ts` (the only implementation, writing through `053`'s repository into an `escalations` collection and notifying nobody), and `escalationHooks.ts` (flushes via `afterSession`, same rationale as `053`'s write path - it's the one per-turn hook that fires inside a `finally`, so a provider outage still flushes). Add the `escalate_to_human` tool (`apps/api/src/tools/escalateToHuman/tool.ts`) with one required, enum-constrained input `reason_category` (`no_tool_for_question`, `customer_asked_for_human`, `out_of_scope_change_request`).
